min_stable_gain.conditions: Tables 1-2 and Fig. 7/8 characterize G = +1 with RS = 100 ohm in series with +IN; p16: 'In unity-gain (G = +1) applications, RS helps to reduce high frequency peaking. It is not needed for any other configurations.'
min_stable_gain.below_minimum: not applicable. No guidance on capacitive (transimpedance) feedback or noise-gain shaping anywhere in the datasheet. p22 (Grounding): 'Stray capacitance on the inverting input and the feedback resistor form a pole, which degrades the phase margin, leading to instability.'

packages_source: p5 Table 4, p6 Table 5, p23, p24
pinout_notes: SOIC: 1 FEEDBACK, 2 -IN, 3 +IN, 4 -VS, 5 NIC, 6 OUTPUT, 7 +VS, 8 NIC, EPAD. LFCSP: 1 NIC, 2 FEEDBACK, 3 -IN, 4 +IN, 5 -VS, 6 NIC, 7 OUTPUT, 8 +VS, EPAD. FEEDBACK is a dedicated pin tied to the output (connection diagrams p1); it sits next to -IN for a short feedback path; using it is optional, the OUTPUT pin can also be used for feedback. The LFCSP pinout separates +IN from -VS to improve HD2 (p19). NIC = no internal connection.
tia_notes: No transimpedance example, figure, table or equation. Only related statements: stray capacitance at the inverting input with RF forms a pole that degrades phase margin (p22); remove ground/power planes under the input and output pins (p22); at unity gain use a short, wide trace from FEEDBACK to -IN (p22).
application_guidance: Fig. 61/62 recommended noninverting/inverting circuits with 0.1 uF + 10 uF bypass on each supply (p16); RS = 100 ohm only at G = +1; RSNUB only for large capacitive loads; 0.1 uF 0508 ceramic plus 10 uF electrolytic bypass, optional bypass between the supplies, minimise vias in supply paths (p22); output noise model and Table 6 output noise: G = +1 3.3, G = +2 7.4, G = +5 16.4, G = +10 31, G = -1 7.4 nV/rtHz (RL = 1 kohm, p18); ADC driver example (AD9244, noise gain 2, p19-p20: SFDR 65.3 dBc, SNR 69.9 dB at 50 MHz); 90 MHz 4-pole Sallen-Key low-pass (p20-p21).
abs_max_and_input_protection: Supply 12.6 V; common-mode input -VS - 0.7 V to +VS + 0.7 V; differential input +/-VS; exposed paddle voltage -VS; power dissipation per Fig. 4; storage -65 to +125 C; operating -40 to +125 C; lead temperature 300 C (10 s); junction 150 C (p5 Table 3). No input clamp or protection diodes are described.
